headline: Analysis and evaluation choices are shown to determine apparent biological effects and method rankings
label: Evaluation Choice Robustness Audits
summary: Eight preprints audit how nulls, permutation units, and evaluation depth drive conclusions in EEG, proteomics, stroke, spatial and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that reported effects and method rankings depend on analytic and evaluation choices, so several preprints add explicit robustness audits. Rich-club analysis in Alzheimer's EEG can show or lose group differences depending on null network construction and hub re-identification. Proteomic co-abundance method rankings shift with evaluation depth, and no method dominates. In drug-tolerant PC9 cells, replicate libraries define the noise floor via a library-level permutation test. Stroke efferocytosis readouts are scored against expression-matched nulls, and the striatal optogenetics reanalysis adds permutation and leave-one-out checks. spicyR v2 offers a permutation-free co-localisation test that corrects image differences. A conditioned sequence model predicts interferon-beta response but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects. What is new is the explicit quantification of how much conclusions move under alternative choices. Not every item is framed as an audit.
